patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Same category, different company size. Choose Ooma only if your buying job matches “SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.” rather than Cisco Webex's shape. Choose Cisco Webex only if your buying job matches “Enterprise UC suite (meetings, messaging, Webex Calling) — Meet/Suite published floors; Ca” rather than Ooma's shape. Workflow advantage: Ooma leans sales-calling; Cisco Webex leans team-communication, contact-center. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Ooma is SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.95 — no annual lock-in.; Cisco Webex is Enterprise UC suite (meetings, messaging, Webex Calling) — Meet/Suite published floors; Calling and Contact Center often quote-layered..
- Company-size focus: Ooma (solo, small-business) vs Cisco Webex (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Ooma-leaning sales-calling vs Cisco Webex-leaning team-communication, contact-center.
- Researched limits: Ooma — SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Cisco Webex — Paid Meet/Suite seat dollars are medium confidence — pricing UI is region/SKU dynamic.

Limitations — Ooma: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus; Cisco Webex: Paid Meet/Suite seat dollars are medium confidence — pricing UI is region/SKU dynamic; Full Calling + Contact Center depth is often EA/quote layered beyond Suite list floors.

Poor-fit cases: Ooma is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited · Cisco Webex is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Paid Meet/Suite seat dollars are medium confidence — pricing UI is region/SKU dynamic · Avoid Ooma if you actually need Cisco Webex's motion (Enterprise UC suite (meetings, messaging, Webex Calling) — Meet/Suite published )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
